claim: The occupational terms in [12iv] (driver, officer “member of police force”, waiter, vicar) are not used as appellations.
evidence_summary: Gee, Officer Krupke, from West Side Story (1957), addresses a police sergeant with Officer + surname. Page 519 already lists the police rank Inspector, and [4ii] has Nurse Fox.
finding: Officer + surname is an appellation in at least American English. The claim holds for driver and waiter.
proposed_wording: The occupational terms in [iv] other than officer are not used as appellations

evidence.passage: §20.5, p. 523. “The occupational terms in [iv] are not used as appellations”.
evidence.establishes: The rank of Krupke shows that officer works as a general police appellation.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.

evidence.example: “‘Gee, Officer Krupke’ is a comedy number from the 1957 musical West Side Story.” The Jets “poke fun at the gruff Police Sergeant Krupke”.
evidence.establishes: A widely known vocative with Officer + surname, applied to a sergeant.
